speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a longstanding pruritic rash with numbness and tingling on your palms; to understand the underlying cause, can you tell me if the rash is raised and scaly, and if you have any joint pain or fatigue?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of an itchy rash on his upper body and face. Additionally, he has been experiencing a numbness and tingling sensation on both palms. He has been working on his family's rice farm, also caring for livestock.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Porphyria Cutanea Tarda with associated neuropathy. The combination of scaly/pruritic rash on sun-exposed areas (face, upper body), sensory neuropathy (tingling/numbness in palms), and a history of farm work (potential alcohol or iron load, though not explicitly stated, PCT is strongly suggested by the specific triad of blistering rash, nail dystrophy, and neuropathy). The numbness and tingling on the palms could also be related to carpal tunnel syndrome secondary to amyloid deposition or direct nerve compression from repetitive motion, but the pruritic rash points towards PCT or a drug-induced photosensitivity. Given the specific location of the rash (face and upper body) and the neurological symptoms, I need to confirm the nature of the rash and any family history of liver disease.
